Single-objective optimization · SETTING 08

Lipschitz convex optimization in a general norm with known convex constraints and exact values

SO_ZO_E06cL

Minimize a globally norm-Lipschitz convex objective over a known convex body using exact scalar values. Matched l1 geometry has an explicit randomized joint dimension-accuracy bracket; other geometries and deterministic regimes retain their own bounds.

Polynomial gap present

01

Setting specification

Task

Minimize $f$ globally over $K$ and return a point with small objective gap.

Admissible model

$B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is a known compact, centrally symmetric convex body with nonempty interior. It induces the norm $\|x\|_B=\inf\{t>0:x\in tB\}$. The set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is known, nonempty, compact and convex.

$f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is globally convex and satisfies $|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|_B$. Constrained minimization is over $K$; boundary minimizers are allowed.

Ball-geometry subregions are written as $K=B_p(0,R)$ and $B=B_q(0,1)$. The exponents $p$ and $q$ describe domain geometry and the regularity norm, respectively. General convex-body specifications do not require this ball parameterization.

Oracle interface

At any finite query point $x$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, the oracle returns the single exact scalar $f(x)$. The reply is uniquely determined and contains no gradient, subgradient or derivative-vector product.

Projection and the stated proximal operations over known geometry are free.

The public inputs are $d$, $B$, $K$, $L$, $\varepsilon$, together with the sets, kernels and auxiliary operations explicitly declared above. Information about the unknown objective and any undisclosed sample distribution is obtained only through the stated interface.

Output

Return $\widehat{x}\in K$. The output may be an unqueried point, an average or convex combination that remains in the stated space. No function value, gradient, inner solution, or accuracy certificate must accompany the output.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The base loss is $\ell(I,x)=f(x)-f_*$, where $f_*=\inf_{u\in K}f(u)$. This nonnegative loss is evaluated at the output, with tolerance $\varepsilon$.

Resource accounting

Each scalar function value or noisy observation costs $1$ call. Every location in a multipoint finite difference, every initialization query, and every reference observation is charged.

Only the declared oracle resource is charged. Computation and storage using existing information, together with explicitly known geometric and proximal operations, are free.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Deterministic

Only deterministic strategies are allowed. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The requirement $\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon$ holds deterministically for each instance.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Randomized

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the instance and external randomness. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The error requirement is $\Pr(\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon)\ge2/3$.

Probability is over the algorithm's random seed only.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Output qualification. Random selection among previously queried points is permitted, subject to the declared success guarantee.

$c_\diamond>0$

$\tau_d$

Boundary between the two randomized lower-bound arguments

Domain
$\tau_d>0$

$\tau_d=c_\diamond/\sqrt{\log(ed)}$.

$d_1^{(1)}$

Sufficient dimension threshold for the matched l1 joint theorem

Domain
$d_1^{(1)}\in\mathbb N$

A fixed integer large enough for Theorem 1, Theorem 2 and Corollary 1, with $d_1^{(1)}\ge\max\{3,m_0\}$ and $d^{-1/2}\le\tau_d<c_0^{(1)}$ for every $d\ge d_1^{(1)}$. No numerical threshold is asserted.

$\mathcal L_{\rm img}$

Previously available image-radius lower envelope with its admissibility guards

Domain
$\mathcal L_{\rm img}\ge0$

$\mathcal L_{\rm img}=\sup\left(\{0\}\cup\left\{c_Z\frac{m\min\{m,(Lr_m/\varepsilon)^2\}}{\log(e\min\{m,(Lr_m/\varepsilon)^2\})}:m_0\le m\le d,\ 0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_ZLr_m\right\}\right)$. An empty set of admissible image dimensions contributes zero.

/proofs/0/body · SHA-256 4468fc6d9bbf4a1ea74651e295f99626443555521dac386c650e090b3f22dbb9
Let $a_B=\max_{\|u\|_2=1}\|u\|_B$ and let $R_2(K)$ be a public Euclidean enclosing radius. Then $\beta_2=a_B^2\beta$, $L_2=a_BL$, and $D_2=a_BR_2(K)$ give the deterministic smooth envelope $$O\!\left(1+\min\{d\sqrt{\beta D_2^2/\varepsilon},d^2\log(e+\beta D_2^2/\varepsilon)\}\right)$$ and Lipschitz localization $O(1+d^2\log(d+1)\log(e+LD_2/\varepsilon))$. The norm inequality $\|v\|_B\le a_B\|v\|_2$ and its dual give the stated Euclidean smoothness and Lipschitz constants. Apply the exact-value Euclidean acceleration or smooth localization theorem with those constants and the public radius; each transformed value remains one scalar call. The global-minimizer promise is retained for the smooth localization argument. For a Lipschitz objective minimized over a known convex set $K$, define $g(x)=f(x)+L_2\operatorname{dist}_2(x,K)$. This is convex and $2L_2$-Lipschitz, $\min g=\min_K f$ on a ball containing $K$, and $f(\Pi_Kx)\le g(x)$. One value of $g$ uses one value of $f$ plus public geometry. The Euclidean ball localization theorem therefore returns a legal point of $K$ after projection. This is a concrete transfer to a general body, not a presumed general-body localization theorem. If $B=UB_2(1)$ and $K=c+RB$ for a public invertible matrix $U$, set $g(y)=f(c+Uy)$. Then $\|Uv\|_B=\|v\|_2$ and $\|U^\top w\|_2=\|w\|_{B,*}$. Thus both the Lipschitz and smoothness budgets are unchanged, the feasible or localization body becomes $B_2(R)$, and one value plus the inverse output map preserves the exact gap, budget, and guarantee. No condition-number factor appears. Deterministic acceleration/localization and randomized two-point methods keep their original algorithm permissions.

/proofs/1/body · SHA-256 1cd2fd44286245db2e01d3873cb88247d0b94a6bed8634b453e4d8636e20dcf0
For an $m$-dimensional Euclidean image radius $r_m(B,K)>0$, smooth and Lipschitz lower bounds may be maximized over the integers $m$ for which their source windows hold. Define $r_m(B,K)$ as the largest radius of a Euclidean ball contained in $AK$, maximized over maps with $\|A\|_{B\to2}\le1$. Dorn et al., Theorem 3.1, gives $$T\ge\max\left\{5m/16,\ (m/4096)\min\{m,\sqrt{\beta r_m^2/\varepsilon}\}\right\},\quad0<\varepsilon\le\beta r_m^2/32.$$ Theorem 3.3, with its regularization parameter zero, gives $$T\ge c_Z\frac{m\min\{m,(Lr_m/\varepsilon)^2\}}{\log(e\min\{m,(Lr_m/\varepsilon)^2\})},\quad m\ge m_Z^\circ,\quad0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_ZLr_m.$$ The all-space nonsmooth transfer uses the source's radial penalty for its homogeneous support-function hard family: a target query is simulated by one bounded source query and known arithmetic, and radial decoding preserves the output comparison. This permits the stronger all-space target queries without silently importing a bounded-query lower bound. For $B=B_q$ and $K=B_p(R)$, put $\theta=(1/2-1/q)_++(1/p-1/2)_+$ and $\gamma=(1/q-1/p)_+$. The source's block certificate is $$r_m\ge R\lfloor d/m\rfloor^\gamma m^{-\theta},\qquad r_d=Rd^{-\theta}.$$ Insert this certificate into each theorem before maximizing over legal $m$. For $q=2$ and $p\le2$, this is $r_m\ge Rm^{-t}$, $t=1/p-1/2$. Other source certificates, such as constant-radius quotient images, may be added only with their own operator-norm and dimension conditions. An exact geometric radius does not itself prove a matching optimization upper bound.

/proofs/2/body · SHA-256 3bea1b77967e9979bba854eff9460c14cc442bdb4d30f8ed47a2c86424b0cb99
The applicable randomized upper bounds are $$O(1+d\sqrt{\eta_{d,s}\beta_2\Theta_s/\varepsilon}),\quad O(1+d\eta_{d,s}\beta_2\Theta_s/\varepsilon),$$ $$O(1+L^2\Theta_s d^{1+2/\min(q,2)-2/s}/\varepsilon^2),\quad O(1+dv_H L_2^2\Theta_H/\varepsilon^2).$$ For the smooth directional methods take $d\ge8$, $1\le s\le2$, $s^*=s/(s-1)$, and $\eta_{d,s}=\min\{s^*-1,16\log d-8\}d^{2/s^*-1}$. Gorbunov, Dvurechensky, and Gasnikov's theorems apply to Euclidean smoothness $\beta_2$ and a prox divergence bounded by $\Theta_s$. Exact noiseless values use batch size one and two scalar values per direction; a finite positive difference scale can be chosen small enough for the fixed budget. For the Lipschitz method of Akhavan et al., $q$ is the regularity norm and $s$ is the prox norm. Their theorem gives expected gap at most $11.9L\sqrt{\Theta_s d^{1+2/\min(q,2)-2/s}/T}$, with two values per round. Tightening the target by a factor three and applying Markov's inequality gives success probability $2/3$. A usable prox is $$t_s=\max\{s,1+1/\log(ed)\},\quad a_{s,d}=\frac{d^{2(1/s-1/t_s)}}{t_s-1},\quad\omega_s(x)=a_{s,d}\|x\|_{t_s}^2/2.$$ It is 1-strongly convex in $\ell_s$ and on $B_p(R)$ has range at most $a_{s,d}R^2d^{2(1/t_s-1/p)_+}/2$. In particular, $q=2$, $s=p\le2$ gives the advertised $a_{p,d}d^{2/p^*}(LR/\varepsilon)^2$ term. For Shamir's general-prox bound let $v_H=(\mathbb E\|U\|_{H,*}^4)^{1/2}$ for a uniform Euclidean sphere direction. Use ball convolution as the smoothed function, with sphere directions in its gradient estimator. The divergence identity belongs to the ball average; this formulation preserves convexity, Lipschitzness, the $O(hL_2)$ smoothing bias, and the source variance proof. All these witnesses are randomized, even when their value oracle is exact and deterministic. For $B=K=B_1(R)$, Euclidean conversion gives $\beta_2=d\beta$, while the $\ell_1$ prox and directional factor contribute $\Theta_1=O(R^2\log(ed))$ and $\eta_{d,1}=O(\log(ed)/d)$. Substitution yields $O(1+d\log(ed)\sqrt{\beta R^2/\varepsilon})$.

/proofs/3/body · SHA-256 3ad958d5da6f01b544d353454c3372bc69148946dc23d87a9f02d9c83e87957c
With ball smoothing $f_h(x)=\mathbb E_{U\sim\operatorname{Unif}(B_2)}f(x+hU)$ and a sphere direction $u$, $$g_h(x)=\frac d{2h}[F(x+hu;Z)-F(x-hu;Z)]u,\quad\mathbb E g_h=\nabla f_h,\quad\mathbb E\|g_h\|^r\le(\sqrt{2d}L)^r.$$ For $r=2$, the bound is $2dL^2$. For each fixed sample, the scalar difference $a(u)=F(x+hu;Z)-F(x-hu;Z)$ is odd on the sphere, hence has mean zero, and has Lipschitz constant at most $2hG$. Sphere Poincare gives $\mathbb E_u a(u)^2\le4h^2G^2/(d-1)$ for $d\ge2$. Thus $\mathbb E_u\|g_h\|^2\le d^2G^2/(d-1)\le2dG^2$; for $d=1$ the difference quotient is directly bounded by $G$. Apply Jensen only to the direction expectation and then integrate over the sample: $$\mathbb E_{Z,u}\|g_h\|^r\le\mathbb E_Z(\mathbb E_u\|g_h\|^2)^{r/2}\le(2d)^{r/2}\mathbb E G^r.$$ No second moment of $G$ is needed when $r<2$. The divergence theorem for ball convolution gives the unbiasedness identity. Integrability follows from the Lipschitz difference bound. Convexity gives $f_h\ge f$, and $|f_h-f|\le hL$; mean strong convexity is preserved on the region where every translated point satisfies it. All statements hold conditionally on the past when the next sample and direction are fresh. Reusing an old adaptively explored sample does not automatically preserve this conditional moment calculation.

/proofs/4/body · SHA-256 685be49a225f461c5aad1c8f1a5c7d6be838d104f66a8c19ee8e9caada27dac4
For a $\mu$-strongly-convex mean with $\mathbb E G^2\le L^2$, $K$ rounds and $T=2K$ scalar calls give $$\mathbb E[f(\bar x_K)-f_*]\le\frac{4dL^2}{\mu(K+1)}+2hL.$$ The merely convex branch uses $O(d(LR/\varepsilon)^2)$ values. Run the paired estimator on $K_h=B_2(R-h)$ and let $x_{h,*}$ minimize $f_h$ there. The shrinkage comparator $y=(1-h/R)x_*$ gives $f_h(y)\le f_*+2hL$. Set $V=2dL^2$, $\eta_t=2/[\mu(t+1)]$, and $D_t=\mathbb E\|x_t-x_{h,*}\|^2$. Projection and strong convexity yield $$\mathbb E[f_h(x_t)-f_h(x_{h,*})]\le\frac{\mu(t-1)}4D_t-\frac{\mu(t+1)}4D_{t+1}+\frac{V}{\mu(t+1)}.$$ Multiply by $t$, telescope, and average with weights $2t/[K(K+1)]$. The initial distance coefficient is zero and the last is nonpositive, giving $2V/[\mu(K+1)]$. Add the comparator error. For expected accuracy choose, for example, $h=\varepsilon/(8L)$ and $K+1\ge8dL^2/(\mu\varepsilon)$. For success probability $2/3$, use $h=\varepsilon/(12L)$ and $K+1\ge24dL^2/(\mu\varepsilon)$, making the expected nonnegative gap at most $\varepsilon/3$ before Markov. For convex objectives, the projected averaging recursion with step $R/\sqrt{VK}$ gives expected optimization error at most $R\sqrt{V/K}$, plus the same smoothing/shrinkage error. Uniform component sampling makes the estimator unbiased for the finite-sum mean and costs exactly two selected-component values per round. Neither the oracle nor the components need be stochastic in that case; the algorithm supplies the randomness. These bounds also hold under an almost-sure Lipschitz promise, since it implies the required second moment. The Gaussian lower construction in the separate lower lemma does not acquire that stronger promise.

/proofs/5/body · SHA-256 1c436f29f6c136a8144171f723bf998d0273e311dc33aeb46b329916be3b6d5f
Retained premises: the frozen common specification gives global L-Lipschitzness in the B norm, known B,K, output in K, and charges scalar objective values. Both views permit deterministic algorithms; randomized g1 requires success at least 2/3. The q1 quantities minimize a nonnegative call budget. For u∈K=c_K+ρB, ||u-c_K||_B≤ρ, hence f(c_K)-f(u)≤Lρ. Taking the infimum over u proves gap≤Lρ. Returning the known center without objective information therefore succeeds deterministically whenever ε≥Lρ, including equality. If ρ=0, K is a singleton and the gap is zero. Nonnegative costs give C*≥0, proving C*=0 in both views. No global-minimizer promise or extra oracle is used. Sharpness for ρ>0: choose a nonzero vector a and normalize it by max_{b∈B}a·b, positive by compactness, symmetry and nonempty interior. Then max_{b∈B}a·b=1 and |a·v|≤||v||_B by the gauge definition. The global convex functions f_±(x)=±La·(x-c_K) are admissible and have minimum -Lρ on K. Their ε-good sets respectively require a·(x-c_K)≤ε/L-ρ and a·(x-c_K)≥ρ-ε/L. These sets are disjoint for ε<Lρ. A zero-call algorithm has the same output distribution on both objectives, so one success probability is at most 1/2. It cannot satisfy deterministic g1 or randomized success 2/3. This last argument proves only nontriviality below the endpoint, not a main-rate lower bound.

Use the exact frozen native comparisons, bounds, proof records and joint ledger listed by the current curator's baseline_refs; no new external theorem is assumed. For a fixed comparison predicate and unchanged quantity, view, guarantee and resource, matching upper/lower zero implies exact complexity zero by nonnegativity. Its canonical main state is optimal and a multiplicative ratio is inapplicable. Matching positive-cost upper/lower orders likewise use optimal; saturation is a separate region property. An alias does not establish any new inequality. Aggregate summary counts are the histogram of these actual native states; missing sides are their union; only logarithmic_gap, polynomial_gap and other_quantified_gap belong to gap_classes. Joint-budget-unclosed is its own special state and does not define a scalar ratio. These are definitions of the existing Atlas status contract, not a new claim about unassessed literature.

/proofs/7/body · SHA-256 29a75cafc0b169b01fc51ddca3f7e33d40543c08270e795734e3aaaf352a0f6d
For $g(z)=f(Rz)/(LR)$, convexity and global l1 Lipschitzness give $|g(z)-g(w)|\le\|z-w\|_1$. A value of $g$ is computed by one value of $f$, and $z\in B_1(1)$ decodes to $Rz\in K$ with the same normalized gap $\alpha_1$. This preserves every pathwise budget and the per-instance seed probability. Lemma 1 of Colombo_KIMI_001 uses exactly $2\lceil576dA_1^2\log(2d)\rceil$ scalar queries and yields expected feasible error at most $\varepsilon/3$. Nonnegativity of the gap and Markov's inequality give success probability at least $2/3$. Its witness is randomized. The public-body value-only theorem in Lemma 2 instead gives a deterministic witness with $O(d^2\log(d+1)\log(4A_1))$ calls; the cited Protasov ingredient is for an explicit known body, with free auxiliary geometric computation. For the source lower bound, ZZQL Theorem 5 applies to a fixed distribution of max-support objectives. Its original Lipschitz constant is 2; divide the functions and their errors by 2. The resulting rows are truncated Gaussian vectors divided by $2\sqrt d$. Their coordinate-coherence event has constant probability uniformly over the legal numbers of rows. Colombo_KIMI_001 Theorem 2 uses the known penalty $\lambda\operatorname{dist}_1(x,B_2(d^{-1/2}))$, with $\lambda=C_{\rm coh}\sqrt{\log(ed)}$. Its decoder sends every feasible output to that inner ball; positive homogeneity answers every finite full-space target query with at most one feasible Euclidean source query. Conditioning costs only the fixed prior probability. Thus its lower bound retains the same all-space oracle, arbitrary output and unrestricted randomized algorithm scope. Set $M_1=\min\{d,A_1^2\}$. For $\alpha_1\le\tau_d$, Theorem 2 yields $c dM_1/[\log(ed)\log(eM_1)]$. Above $\tau_d$, Corollary 1 gives $d/[16384\log(ed)]$. There $A_1^2<\log(ed)/c_\diamond^2$, so the ratio of the two-point upper to the latter lower is $O(A_1^2\log^2(ed))=O(\log^3(ed))$ for fixed source constants. For $\alpha_1\le d^{-1/2}\le\tau_d$, $M_1=d$ and the regional lower is $\Omega(d^2/\log^2(ed))$, independent of any further accuracy refinement. Theorem 1 also gives the weaker but uniform expression $a dM_1/\Lambda_1^2$ over the complete stated small-accuracy domain. Every admissible image-radius lower inequality remains valid. Taking its supremum with zero gives $\mathcal L_{\rm img}$, and taking its maximum with the new applicable lower cannot weaken the bracket. In particular, a previously available finer-accuracy image lower is not discarded. The upper envelope is the minimum of applicable algorithms under the same guarantee. On the fixed-$c$ slice $\alpha_1=c/\sqrt d$, with $c>0$ fixed, $dM_1=d^2\min\{1,c^{-2}\}$ and $\Lambda_1=O_c(\log(ed))$, giving a new $\Omega_c(d^2/\log^2(ed))$ lower while retaining the existing $O_c(d^2\log(ed))$ randomized upper. A lower bound for all randomized algorithms also holds for deterministic algorithms. The deterministic upper is only the deterministic known-body method; the randomized two-point witness is not used in that view. Consequently the deterministic fine-accuracy region is near optimal, whereas its coarse-accuracy bracket retains the explicitly displayed polynomial factor.

/joint_analysis/impact/2/validity_region · SHA-256 8ac3b850aefa1115a150e653472c5f992cf22de042ffec1212c0c25096dc1d16
For each registered deterministic/randomized g1 q1 quantity: d∈N, d≥1; known compact centrally symmetric convex B with nonempty interior; known nonempty compact convex K; L>0, ε>0; globally convex L-Lipschitz objectives on R^d; unrestricted exact scalar queries, output in K, and the registered fixed-path budget. Geometry varies jointly and its dependence remains explicit. Native p,q,R are conditional ball coordinates. The historical R metadata about a global minimizer cannot override the fixed constrained contract; the new endpoint uses derived ρ. Deterministic q2 remains separate and untransferred. Write Z for K=c_K+ρB, ρ≥0, ε≥Lρ within this domain.

/joint_analysis/impact/3/validity_region · SHA-256 8ac3b850aefa1115a150e653472c5f992cf22de042ffec1212c0c25096dc1d16
For each registered deterministic/randomized g1 q1 quantity: d∈N, d≥1; known compact centrally symmetric convex B with nonempty interior; known nonempty compact convex K; L>0, ε>0; globally convex L-Lipschitz objectives on R^d; unrestricted exact scalar queries, output in K, and the registered fixed-path budget. Geometry varies jointly and its dependence remains explicit. Native p,q,R are conditional ball coordinates. The historical R metadata about a global minimizer cannot override the fixed constrained contract; the new endpoint uses derived ρ. Deterministic q2 remains separate and untransferred. Write Z for K=c_K+ρB, ρ≥0, ε≥Lρ within this domain.

/joint_analysis/target/full_domain · SHA-256 3f4d2fca87d63c4fb83a0e0750a141c20e6c1a0bc6edebfefc0f4d9bdff3e644
For each registered deterministic/randomized g1 q1 quantity: d∈N, d≥1; known compact centrally symmetric convex B with nonempty interior; known nonempty compact convex K; L>0, ε>0; globally convex L-Lipschitz objectives on R^d; unrestricted exact scalar queries, output in K, and the registered fixed-path budget. Geometry varies jointly and its dependence remains explicit. Native p,q,R are conditional ball coordinates. R is the public radius only in an explicit feasible-body parameterization; the matching-body endpoint uses derived ρ. Deterministic q2 remains separate and untransferred. Write Z for K=c_K+ρB, ρ≥0, ε≥Lρ within this domain.

On matching bodies K=c_K+ρB, ρ≥0 is the unique homothety scale derived from B,K; c_K is the known symmetry center, or the sole point when ρ=0. For ρ>0, g(u)=f(c_K+ρu)/(Lρ) is 1-Lipschitz, so ε/(Lρ) is dimensionless accuracy. No global-minimizer promise is used.
